title: Autumn Song of the Harvest Moon (Sur Ka Synrai)
cultural_context: Lyrical ode celebrating autumn (Ka Synrai) when golden paddy waves on terrace fields and the harvest moon shines, from 'Ka Tragoidia Bad Ki Poim'.

khasi: Ka synrai ka la wan ha ka ri,
U kba u la ih ha ki pynthor;
U phalang kum ka ksiar ba tyngshain,
Haba ka lyer ka pyrsad jai-jai;
Ki nongrep ki kmen ban ot kba,
Ha ryngkat ka sur ba sawa kynjai;
Ki theh ia ka ja sotti ba thiang
Ban pynkmen ia ki tnum baroh.
english: Autumn has arrived upon our hills,
The paddy stands ripe in golden terraces;
Shimmering like molten gold in the sun,
When gentle breezes sweep the fields;
The cultivators rejoice to reap the harvest,
Bringing joy to every village home.

khasi: U bnai synrai u phyrnai ha suiñ,
U pynshai ia ki khlaw bad ki wah;
Ki khun ki kti ki ia kmen lang,
Ban burom ia U Blei Nongbuh;
Kupar ba kynrei ngi la ioh,
Na ka kpoh jong ka Meiramew;
Ngin ri ia ka hok bad ka jingsuk
Haduh ba ka sngi kan wai.
english: The autumn moon gleams bright in the sky,
Families and kindred gather in gladness,
To venerate God, the Great Giver of Life;
From the fertile womb of Mother Earth;
We shall safeguard righteousness and peace
Until our allotted days are complete.
